document.title: Afghanistan: Reported Activities of Extremist Arabs and Pakistanis Since August 20 U.S. Strike on Khost Terrorist Camps
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), 1998 Missile Strikes on Bin Laden May Have Backfired
document.note: [Confidential] Tracks Arabs and Pakistanis expelled from Khost. Bin Laden is keeping a low profile, probably in Kandahar, where he has stayed at Mullah Omar's residence and is thought to have been ordered to stay close to Omar; many of his followers are moving to Kabul. The strikes reportedly killed about 20 Pakistanis and 15 Arabs. Excised.

events.description: Taliban captured Mazar-i-Sharif; 11 Iranian officials went missing, allegedly executed by SSP volunteers.
US missile strikes on Khost terrorist camps; at least 50 reportedly killed including about 20 Pakistanis and 15 Arabs.
Attack on two UN expatriates in Kabul, one fatally; Taliban said two Pakistanis were arrested in Kandahar.
Embassy meeting with Afghan moderate in Peshawar alleging SSP killed Iranians and about 60 others.
The Muslim reported bodies of eight JUI-F members returned to Pakistan.
Meeting with Afghan resistance commander on Bin Ladin's location; cable sent.
Taliban capture Mazar-i-Sharif; eleven Iranian officials go missing, allegedly executed by SSP volunteers.
U.S. missile strike on Khost terrorist camps; at least 50 reportedly killed, including about 20 Pakistanis and 15 Arabs.
Attack on two UN expatriates in Kabul, one dead of gunshot wounds; alleged HUM involvement; Taliban arrested two Pakistanis.
Meeting in Peshawar with a moderate Afghan alleging SSP killed the Iranians, Afghan staff and neighbors (~60 killed).
Meetings with sources reporting Arabs moving from Khost to Kabul and bin Ladin in Kandahar.
The Muslim reported that bodies of eight Pakistani JUI-F members killed fighting in Afghanistan were returned to Pakistan for burial.
U.S. Embassy Islamabad cable assessing that U.S. strikes flushed Arab and Pakistani militants out of Khost for the time being.
Busses of Pakistani volunteers for the Taliban reported crossing at Torkham and Chaman; pro-Taliban religious leaders recruiting madrassa students.

key_claims: Arab and Pakistani extremists reportedly left Khost after the 20 August 1998 US strikes.
Bin Ladin reportedly stays in Kandahar, kept under watch by Mullah Omar and the Taliban.
Unconfirmed reports implicate SSP volunteers in the execution of 11 Iranian officials at Mazar-i-Sharif.
Rumors link HUM to the UN expatriate killing in Kabul, though the Taliban said the attackers were Pakistanis arrested in Kandahar.
Pakistani volunteers continue to cross at Torkham and Chaman; 20-40 percent of Taliban forces may be Pakistani.
Eight JUI-F members killed in Afghanistan were returned to Pakistan for burial.
The UN doubts the Taliban are willing to control their extremist allies.
